paper.title_en: LIGHT01: A prototype LGAD pixel readout ASIC for picosecond timing measurements in 28 nm CMOS technology
paper.abstract_en: Precision timing has become a central requirement for future high-luminosity collider detectors, where large pile-up densities require four-dimensional event reconstruction. This paper presents LIGHT01, a first-generation LGAD pixel readout ASIC designed in 28 nm CMOS technology for picosecond timing applications. The chip targets possible future CMS timing-detector concepts and is optimized for hybrid integration with trench-isolated LGAD sensors. LIGHT01 integrates an 8 × 8 pixel matrix, charge-sensitive front-end amplifiers, fast discriminators, per-pixel time-to-digital converters, Time-over-Threshold-based time-walk correction, programmable biasing, calibration circuitry, SPI control, and zero-suppressed readout. The design targets <math altimg="si15.svg" display="inline" id="d1e439"><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>100</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> pixels, an input capacitance of approximately 0.2 pF, and a timing resolution below 30 ps RMS. Post-layout simulations indicate an expected timing resolution of approximately 24 ps RMS around a minimum-ionizing-particle equivalent charge of about 70 ke<math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e459"><msup><mrow/><mrow><mo>−</mo></mrow></msup></math>(including the multiplication of the LGAD sensor). The ASIC architecture, reconstruction algorithm, calibration strategy, expected performance, and experimental validation infrastructure are discussed.
